subject: FintechCo: Regional pricing follow-up (US vs EU)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — token volumes and regional pricing

Hi Asha — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can get a proper quote over to you: 

1) Estimated token volumes: you mentioned 200M tokens/month for baseline traffic and a peak pattern that could reach ~1.2B tokens in month 3 after launch. Please confirm whether these numbers represent input only, output only, or combined (you said combined but I want to be precise).

2) Target unit economics: you said the finance team is looking at a target of ~$1,000 per 1M tokens (target $/1M). I flagged that as a target benchmark — is that firm or a range?

3) Regional residency & cost impact: you noted a preference for EU data residency for EU customers. Two points we want to confirm: (a) do you require all inference for EU users to stay in EU regions (not just storage), and (b) are you ok with a hybrid approach where low-latency EU traffic is served from EU with a modest regional premium?

Next steps I propose: 
- You confirm input/output token split and whether the 200M/1.2B are combined.
- We’ll run a quick unit-econ sim (US vs EU) and send a 1-page pricing comparison + XLS with sensitivity to model choice and batching assumptions.
- If the numbers look reasonable, book a 30-min follow-up to align on procurement timelines and data residency controls.

I attached an example token estimate sheet (FintechCo_token_estimates.xlsx) and a short US vs EU pricing note (redwood_pricing_us-eu.pdf).

Happy to hop on a call this week — my calendar: https://calendly.com/dylan-redwood/30

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Asha Patel <asha@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — token volumes and regional pricing

Thanks Dylan — great recap. A few clarifications: 

- Token split: the numbers I gave are combined (input + output). Our rough expectation is 60% output / 40% input once the product stabilizes.
- Budget: the $1,000 per 1M tokens is our internal target, but finance has said they can stretch to $1,250/1M for the first 3 months if we can show clear latency/SLA benefits.
- Residency: EU customers must have inference for EU users stay in EU (both processing and short-term caches). We are open to hybrid for non-EU users.

Please include a version that shows the delta if we require strict EU-only serving for EU traffic vs hybrid routing. Also include any onboarding/one-time fees and estimated monthly minimums.

We’re trying to get a procurement window in May — if you can provide a firm quote and a short SOC2/data-residency appendix by 4/23 that would be ideal.

Best,
Asha
Head of Product, FintechCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FintechCo pricing follow-up (internal)

Looping in Sean since procurement & discounts likely live with him. Summary for quote: 

- Baseline: 200M combined tokens/month -> with 60/40 split that is 120M output / 80M input. Peak: up to 1.2B combined.
- Target price: FintechCo target $1,000/1M; willing to accept $1,250/1M for first 3 months.
- Residency constraint: EU inference must remain in EU regions (no cross-region serving for EU users).

Pricing asks for internal discussion: 
- Provide two SKU stacks: (A) Hybrid routing (default US serving, EU traffic routed to EU when beneficial) with a modest regional premium on EU tokens (we typically see ~+20–35% cost uplift in EU depending on instance availability and licensing). (B) Strict EU-only serving for EU traffic which typically increases unit cost due to smaller capacity pools and potential reserved capacity premium — estimate +30–60% on EU-served tokens.
- Show sensitivity to batching (continuous batching reduces per-token CPU/GPU cost) and to a conservative cache hit rate (prefix caching can reduce output tokens for repeated prompts).

Sean — can you provide a quick sketch of list vs committed pricing options and a recommended discount band for a first-year commit that hits 1.2B peak (assume committed baseline of 400M/month)?

I’ll assemble the customer-facing quote once we have Sean’s guidance and the econ sim.

- Marissa
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@fintechco.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FintechCo: Regional pricing follow-up (US vs EU)

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear constraints. Quick take and next steps below. 

1) Unit economics (high level examples) — assuming mixed model family (open model + quantized):
   - US-served tokens: list price equivalence ~ $0.90–$1,100 per 1M tokens depending on batching and cache.
   - EU-served tokens (hybrid routing): ~ +25% uplift -> roughly $1,125–$1,375 per 1M.
   - EU strict residency (reserved capacity): ~ +40% uplift on top of US baseline -> roughly $1,260–$1,540 per 1M.

2) Discount bands: for a committed baseline of 400M/month (12-month commit) we can offer an initial 15% commitment discount off list per-token unit rates, with an additional 5% accelerated volume credit once monthly usage > 800M for two consecutive months. We’ll model first-quarter ramp pricing to align to your $/1M targets.

3) One-time/onboarding: Professional services for EU deployment and SOC2/data-residency attestation work typically $12k–$25k depending on complexity. We’ll call this out as a line item.

4) Deliverables & timing: I’ll attach a short Excel with the econ sim and two scenario PDFs (hybrid vs strict EU). We’ll include exposure lines for model choice and cache assumptions. Expect the formal quote and attachments by tomorrow 4/23 EOD.

If that timing works, I’ll include a procurement-friendly summary table and a DocuSign-ready T& C for review.

Thanks — Sean
VP, Sales, Redwood Inference
